note: `referencePng` is drawn by the Devup Bridge plugin when one serves the file, so a reference image no longer needs login or spends Figma allowance, and the plugin never refuses it. `get_screenshot` draws the node in its ancestors' context - their paints, clipping, opacity, blend modes, layer blur and drop shadow - with every other layer left out, across the node's render bounds; the plugin exports those bounds the same way (`useAbsoluteBounds: false`; scale 1 with the longer edge held to 8192px like the direct path's `maxDimension`, sRGB). Where no other layer draws into the area, the canvas export (`contentsOnly: false`) is that picture and the bridge flattens it onto the page background. Where one does, the plugin exports the node alone (`contentsOnly: true`) and describes its ancestors, and devup-mcp composes the rest: solid, gradient and image (PNG, JPEG, GIF) paints, rounded clipping, the eighteen blend modes, alpha and luminance masks, layer blur, drop shadows (spread included, and cut away under a layer that does not show its shadow behind it), inner shadows, a rectangle-like ancestor's stroke (solid or gradient, undashed, mitred), and an ancestor's and the node's own background blur. A mask is exported by its box, which Figma gives it in place of render bounds, and a node inside a mask's own layers is not drawn, as get_screenshot leaves it out. An image fill devup-mcp does not decode (not a PNG, JPEG or GIF, over 8192 pixels on an edge, or mostly metadata) is decoded by the plugin's UI as a browser does and handed back as a PNG laid out at the original's size; the UI decodes one image at a time, a scene's images share 20 seconds for it, and an image whose conversion would take over 512 MiB, or one left when the time is up, goes as it is. Swept over the 225 scanned nodes of the devup Test file with the direct path unreachable, every node composes or takes the canvas without a note. What it cannot compose (another ancestor's stroke - not a rectangle's, dashed, round- or bevel-joined outside or centred, or painted otherwise -, a background blur taking in what lies below on a layer inside the node or on a node that cannot hold children or has a stroke, image fills with rotation or filters, other paints, effects it does not know such as noise or texture, a drop shadow cast from farther than the margin drawn around the area (its offset and spread past 512 pixels), areas over 8M pixels, images over 64 MiB together, a composition that would take over 1.5 GiB or four billion blur and shadow-spread kernel taps - counted before it is drawn, the masks each layer keeps and the decoding of every picture and image counted from their headers before any decoder is made included (PNG and GIF decoders held to that allowance, with what a PNG decoder keeps outside it - unfiltered rows, an entry per text chunk - counted too, a JPEG counted with its coefficient buffers at its sampling factors and the copies of its bytes, and one with a marker standing alone before its frame header (another SOI, a restart, a stuffed zero) refused; an image the plugin's UI did not hand back as a PNG and that is not a PNG, JPEG or GIF (WebP among them), is a PNG wider than 8192 pixels, or does not decode within its allowance as a PNG or GIF, is not decoded) - a part the plugin could not export, or a composition that stopped unexpectedly) is drawn as the canvas shows it with the reason and the layers reaching in as `referencePngNote`, which resource delivery keeps; with the direct path logged in, `get_screenshot` answers instead. Drawn from its own paints and children, a node is still cut by its mask, its background blur included. Answers over 6 MiB are held by the plugin and read in 4 MiB pieces, as ASCII so offsets agree on both sides; a held answer stays until read or two minutes pass and is never evicted by another request. While held answers reach 192 MiB (where new pictures stop being taken, not a ceiling) the plugin answers `DEVUP_REFERENCE_PNG_BUSY` and the bridge asks again for up to 45 seconds; an answer that vanished before it was read is fetched once more; one that would exceed 90 MiB (under the 96 MiB the bridge reads back) drops the composition and carries the canvas picture with the reason. Measured against `get_screenshot` on the devup Test file: six composed nodes within 2/255 on 99.65% to 99.97% of pixels and at most 15/255 apart from the clipped rim of a blurred ancestor (84/255 on 0.19%); eleven harness screens within 2/255 on at least 99.98% (the photo grid 90.5%, at most 37/255); the render harness scored each screen within 0.02 points either way. The plugin manifest declares `enablePrivatePluginApi`, which Figma requires before it fills `figma.fileKey`. A plugin built before this devup-mcp answers `DEVUP_BRIDGE_UNKNOWN_SCRIPT`; that read goes to the direct path when the plugin reported the file's key and the direct path is logged in, and otherwise the plugin's answer comes back with what to do instead of a login prompt. An asset too large to send says how large it was. Update the plugin checkout and run the plugin again to get the new reads.
